cr_data.provenance: Caroline Keck, Cooperstown, NY, gift, 1940s; Foundation for Conservation, gift, 1982; (Peter H. Davidson & Co., New York, NY) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1946. . . . On backing: 1924. Note: O'Keeffe told me she was going to destroy this as it is cracked." Backing inscription, Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, Downtown Gallery Archive, date 1924? See cat. nos. 370–72, 547, 612, 613. Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Destroyed by Keck for experiment." O'Keeffe gave work to Caroline Keck for experimentation purposes in the 1940s and, in 1981, gave her permission to restore the work and donate it to the Foundation for Conservation so that it could be sold to raise funds for the Foundation. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Rough, mountain-like gray forms run along the bottom of this abstract work. Rolling above these are fluffy, pale pink and white shapes similar to layered clouds. On the lefthand side of the frame, the cloud-like forms open up to reveal a dark, cavern-like circular shape.
title: Skunk Cabbage
